finding.claim: The ext:: remote-helper protocol check is bypassed when the first character after '::' is a newline, because the regex (.+)::.+ does not match newlines. An attacker-controlled clone URL can then reach git's remote-helper mechanism.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled URL passed to Repo.clone_from (or Remote.create/set_url, or refspecs to fetch/pull/push) with default allow_unsafe_protocols=False
finding.sink: git clone -- <url> (git/repo/base.py:1541), which may spawn git-remote-ext

trace.note: polish_url only replaces backslashes; newlines untouched
re_unsafe_protocol = re.compile(r'(.+)::.+') -- '.' does not match newline
match = re_unsafe_protocol.match(url); no match for 'ext::\n...' so check passes
git.clone(multi, '--', clone_url, ...) runs with the unchecked URL

finding.guards_checked: Regex-only protocol check (cmd.py:957); polish_url with expand_vars=False (no newline handling); '--' separator (does not affect remote-helper routing). Git's protocol.allow default may still permit ext for user-initiated invocations. Same check guards remote.py:661, 813, 1071, 1128, 1204. NOT verified at runtime: no shell available; needs a test on the target git version with a harmless command.

finding.claim: Remote.pull never inspects refspecs for option-like values. A refspec beginning with --upload-pack= may be forwarded to git fetch as an option, where it can execute a command, if git pull does not insert '--' before forwarded refspecs.
finding.source: Refspec string passed to Remote.pull(refspec=...), e.g. a user-supplied branch name
finding.sink: git pull -- <remote> <refspec> (git/remote.py:1136-1137); refspec forwarded to git fetch argv

trace.note: only check_unsafe_protocols(ref) is applied to refspecs
_option_candidates only collects args starting with '-'; none are supplied here
self.repo.git.pull('--', self, refspec, ...) -- refspec after remote, outside option parsing

finding.guards_checked: check_unsafe_protocols on refs (remote.py:1126-1128); kwargs-only option check (remote.py:1130-1134); '--' separator before remote. Fetch (remote.py:1079-1080) and push (remote.py:1212-1213) are not affected: fetch's '--' precedes positional args, and push sends refspecs over the transport. Git pull's internal forwarding to fetch is NOT verified; the missing refspec check is certain, exploitability depends on git's behavior. Declared unsafe in remote.py:543-546.

finding.claim: Git subprocesses run with the configuration of whatever repository directory the application opens. A repo-controlled core.fsmonitor command, or a core.hooksPath (which may be absolute) pointing to an arbitrary executable, is executed with no GitPython-side override.
finding.source: Contents of .git/config (core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath) in an untrusted repository directory that the application opens via Repo(path), e.g. a customer-uploaded .git directory
finding.sink: Any repo.git.<cmd> subprocess (git/cmd.py Git.execute) triggering core.fsmonitor; index.commit() running the hook from core.hooksPath (git/index/fun.py:68-75 and run_commit_hook around 95-110)

trace.note: hooks_dir = config.get('core','hooksPath', fallback='') read from repo config
abspath(join(working_dir, expanduser(hooks_dir), name)); absolute hooks_dir overrides the join
Git.execute spawns git with the repo's local config in effect; no -c core.fsmonitor=false or safe.directory override

finding.guards_checked: Grep for fsmonitor, safe.directory and core.hooksPath found no GitPython-side overrides. Git's own safe.directory only covers ownership mismatches, so a same-user uploaded repository is not protected. Exploitability depends on the application opening untrusted repositories. Under Semgrep policy this is a trust-boundary item to flag to Security (the security team).
